Applicant :- Babloo Gaur
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Gauri Shankar Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Sri Imran Khan, learned Aga, for the State, apprised the Court that notice has been served to the
informant of the case on 4.12.2023.
2. Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

3. Heard Sri Gauri Shankar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Imran Khan, learned
Aga, for the State.
4. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release
him on bail in Case Crime No.225 of 2023, under Sections 376 Ab, 504 and 506 Ipc and Section 5/6
Pocso Act, Police Station Dumariyaganj, District Siddharth Nagar during pendency of the trial.
5. Fir of the present case was lodged against the applicant and according to the Fir, applicant tried

to commit rape upon the daughter of the informant aged about 6 years.
6.

sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that entire allegation made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and as informant has borrowed Rs. 12,500/- from the applicant and when applicant demanded back his money then instead of returning the money, he implicated him in the present matter.
7.

He further submits that however victim in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. stated that applicant tried to commit rape upon her but her story does not appear to be convincing and it appears that under the pressure of the informant she stated against the applicant and no reliance can be placed on such child witness.
8. He further submits that applicant is not having any previous criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 25.9.2023.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayerfor bail and submits that allegations made against the applicant are serious in nature and he tried to commit rape upon the minor daughter of the informant aged about 6 years and victim in her statements categorically stated against the applicant and applicant could not bring any good reason for his false implication, therefore, he should not be released on bail.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. As per allegation applicant tried to commit rape upon a child aged about six years and child in her both the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. categorically stated that after removing her lower applicant also removed his lower and touched his organ at her vagina and tried to commit rape.

12. I find force in the argument advanced by learned AGA that the conduct of the applicant as per allegation appears to be highly objectionable and applicant is detained for offence under Section 376AB IPC along with Section 5/6 POCSO Act in which minimum punishment is 20 years.

13. Applicant, however, has taken defence in paragraph-26 to the affidavit filed in support of the instant bail application that due to money, dispute arose between him and informant, therefore, he was falsely implicated by the informant in the present matter but the defence taken by applicant appears to be vague and general in nature and in my view, on the basis of such defence statement of the victim cannot be completely brushed aside at this stage.
14. Further, applicant in the present matter is in jail for hardly 2-1/2 months.

15. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is not entitled to be released on bail at this stage.
16. Accordingly, the instant bail application is rejected at this stage.
